# security-openbao-raft-snapshot

<!-- BEGIN DECLARED (generated by scripts/wiki-compile.py — do not edit) -->

> Source comment, verbatim from `kustomization.yaml`:
>
> OpenBao raft snapshots — applied on top of security/openbao via components:
>
> Adds:
> - CronJob openbao-raft-snapshot: `bao operator raft snapshot save` every 6 h
> into PVC openbao-snapshots, keeping the newest SNAPSHOT_KEEP files (default 28 = 7 days)
> - PVC openbao-snapshots (1Gi, no storageClassName)
>
> Put the snapshot volume somewhere other than the data PVC (another disk, node
> or NFS). Unlike raft data, snapshots are plain files and NFS is fine here.
> A snapshot on the volume it protects is not a backup.
>
> This component never ships the token. The tenant supplies Secret
> openbao-snapshot-token with key `token`. scripts/openbao/bootstrap.sh writes the
> least-privilege policy `raft-snapshot` (policies/raft-snapshot.hcl: read
> sys/storage/raft/snapshot). Create a periodic token the job renews on every run,
> so it never expires while the job keeps running:
> bao token create -policy=raft-snapshot -orphan -period=720h -field=token
> kubectl -n security create secret generic openbao-snapshot-token --from-literal=token=<token>
>
> Usage in overlay kustomization.yaml:
> resources:
> - path/to/security/openbao
> components:
> - path/to/security/openbao/raft-snapshot
>
> Restore (the instance must be initialized and unsealed). Mount the snapshot PVC in
> a throwaway pod (restricted PSA, BAO_ADDR=http://openbao:8200, BAO_TOKEN from a
> root or sudo token). Wait until `bao status` answers (a new pod can be refused for a
> few seconds), then run:
> bao operator raft snapshot restore -force /snapshots/openbao-<ts>.snap
> -force is needed when the target was initialized separately (e.g. after wiping the
> data PVC and running `bao operator init` again). The restore replaces everything,
> token store included: afterwards the root token and recovery keys are the ones
> from the cluster the snapshot was taken on, not the freshly initialized ones.
> With seal-static, Secret openbao-seal-key must hold the same key the snapshot was
> taken under. With Shamir, the unseal keys of the snapshot's cluster apply.
>
> Tenant overlay can patch:
> - schedule (default "0 */6 * * *")
> - SNAPSHOT_KEEP env of the CronJob
> - PVC storage class and size
> - image (keep it equal to the StatefulSet's; a tenant `images:` entry covers both)
>
> Pod Security: runs under the `restricted` profile.
>
> No `namespace:` here on purpose. A Component's namespace applies to everything the
> consuming kustomization holds, not only to its own resources: it would move a
> tenant's other resources into `security`. The resources below carry
> `namespace: security` themselves, like the base, and a tenant overlay's
> `namespace:` moves them along with it.
